wordmark.purpose: The Crest brand mark only - sidebar and login screen. Never reused for a heading.

body.purpose: Default for every table cell, form value, and paragraph of UI copy.

label.purpose: Table column headers, stat card labels, form field labels - the uppercase-tracked tier.

shadows.name: card-elevation
shadows.value: var(--theme-card-shadow) - dark presets: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(text1,0.06), 0 10px 24px -8px rgba(bg,0.55), 0 3px 8px -3px rgba(bg,0.4); light presets: 0 1px 2px rgba(text1,0.06), 0 10px 24px -8px rgba(text1,0.1)
shadows.purpose: Uniform policy shadow on every .card/.stat-card, added 2026-07-12 - retired the old flat-by-default model. Generated per-preset from that preset's own bg/text1 (or accent, for Bright) so the shadow's cast color matches the theme instead of flattening to generic black. Background-lightness shift is still the primary depth cue; this is a secondary layer, not a decoration budget - don't invent a stronger version to mean 'important'.

shadows.name: floating-action
shadows.purpose: For content genuinely fixed above the page (e.g. the bottom-anchored Fab / cart button) - unchanged since before the elevation model rewrite.

shadows.name: live-pulse-ring
shadows.purpose: Breathing ring animation on elements needing real-time attention (new order banner, live badge). Uses the relevant signal color's own alpha - unchanged since before the elevation model rewrite.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The one formalized easing curve, used for sidebar nav hover/active transitions.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Duration paired with ease-standard for sidebar interactions.

motion.name: button-transition
motion.purpose: Default button/tab/badge state-change speed. No bounce, no elastic, no transform-on-press.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single call-to-action button style. Accent background, theme-paired foreground, 700 weight, 12px radius.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; border: none; background: var(--theme-accent); color: var(--theme-accent-text); transition: background 0.13s, color 0.13s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--theme-accent-hover); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--theme-focus-ring); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The default secondary/tertiary action button - quiet until hovered. Same 12px radius as Primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; background: var(--theme-input-bg); color: var(--theme-text1); border: 1px solid var(--theme-border-lt); transition: background 0.13s, color 0.13s, border-color 0.13s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--theme-table-hover); border-color: var(--theme-accent); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Alpha-tinted status chip, 8px radius. Shown here in the success variant; danger/warning/gray follow the same shape with their own signal color - never a solid fill with white text.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-transform: capitalize; } .ds-badge-green { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.10); color: var(--theme-green); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base surface for grouped content - 18px radius, one tone lighter than the page, plus the per-preset card-elevation shadow (see extensions.shadows) added 2026-07-12. Depth is background-shift + border + shadow now, not border-only.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--theme-card); border: 1px solid var(--theme-border); border-radius: 18px; padding: 24px; box-shadow: var(--theme-card-shadow); } .ds-card-title { margin: 0 0 8px; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--theme-text3); } .ds-card-value { margin: 0; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--theme-text1); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Labeled form field with the theme-colored focus ring, 12px radius - label always sits above, never a placeholder standing in for it.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--theme-text2); letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-field-input { background: var(--theme-input-bg); border: 1px solid var(--theme-border); border-radius: 12px; padding: 9px 12px; font-size: 13px; color: var(--theme-text1); outline: none; transition: border-color 0.14s; } .ds-field-input:focus { border-color: var(--theme-accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--theme-focus-ring); } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: var(--theme-text3); }

narrative.overview: Crest Suite is operated, not visited. An owner is checking margin between service rushes; an accountant is reconciling TDS figures before a filing deadline. Neither has time for the interface to perform. The system is built around legibility under pressure: dense tables that stay scannable, a single restrained accent, and status communicated through color and position rather than decoration. This deliberately rejects two things named in PRODUCT.md: the dated, hierarchy-less density of legacy Nepali ERP software, and the templated purple-gradient look of generic AI-generated SaaS. The product runs across ten interchangeable theme presets (dark charcoal-and-gold is the shipped default; Bright, a crisp cool-blue light theme, is the newest), all built from the same token set; every rule is written against the default preset's values, but the relationships between tokens hold across all ten, even where literal shape/shadow values don't.
keyCharacteristics: Depth comes primarily from a one-step background-lightness shift, with a per-preset shadow as a secondary cue (elevation model rewritten 2026-07-12 - previously flat-only, shadows are now uniform policy on every card, not a decoration budget)
One accent color per screen, applied sparingly, never as a wash - Bright's ClientDashboard.jsx KPI badges are the one named, scoped exception
A serif wordmark is the one deliberate ornamental choice in an otherwise all-sans, all-functional system
Status is color-coded consistently, with a rationed 4th color (purple) reserved for genuine 4th/5th categories

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Aged Brass is the only non-semantic color on any screen. If a second brand color shows up anywhere outside the rationed purple exception, it's a mistake, not a design choice. A 2026-08-05 audit found a second undocumented accent (an indigo/blue, #60a5fa/#818cf8) had spread into three files across two separate sessions before being caught - treat any unfamiliar saturated color next to Aged Brass as a near-certain instance of this drift, not a one-off.

rules.name: The Accent-Text Pairing Rule
rules.body: Any element with an Aged-Brass background uses the theme's paired accent-text token for its foreground, never a hardcoded white or black - the accent color changes per theme preset and a hardcoded foreground will fail contrast on at least one of the ten. Shipped and fixed twice as a real bug (a FAB label, then an admin page's badge) - on its second recurrence, treat any hardcoded #000/#fff next to var(--theme-accent) as the bug on sight.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Georgia appears exactly once per screen (the wordmark, if visible at all). Never used for a heading, callout, or emphasis.

rules.name: Card elevation is uniform policy, not a decoration budget
rules.body: Every card gets the same per-preset card-elevation shadow (see extensions.shadows). This retired the old Flat-By-Default Rule (2026-07-12). Don't invent a stronger or different shadow to mean 'important' or 'premium' - floating-action and live-pulse-ring are the only two shadows that still carry extra meaning.

rules.name: Badges are alpha-tint, never solid fill
rules.body: Each semantic color renders as a ~10-12% alpha tint of itself as background, full-opacity as text - never a solid fill with white text. Found and fixed as a real recurrence on an admin page's Trial Accounts panel (2026-08-05).

dos: Do use the theme's accent-text token as the foreground on any accent-colored background
Do keep tonal alpha-tints at 2-18% opacity
Do wrap every wide table in the horizontal-scroll container
Do reserve the rationed 4th color (purple) for a genuine 4th/5th categorical need
Do put labels above form fields, always
donts: Don't build dense, hierarchy-less layouts in the name of fitting more in
Don't reach for purple gradients, Inter-everywhere, or a templated hero-plus-three-cards layout
Don't invent a stronger/different shadow to mean important or premium - card elevation is uniform policy now, not a decoration budget
Don't hardcode white or black as text on an accent background
Don't use a second saturated brand color alongside Aged Brass on the same screen
